title: A Bell in the Snow

plate.narration: A little snowhorn goat bleats across the meltwater. Its herd answers from a snowy ledge, bells clinking. Between them, the water runs cold and quick. Those small hooves need a way home.

goal.text: Get the little goat home safe and find somewhere warm.

steps.label: Get the goat back to its herd
Get everyone in from the cold

arrival.narration: The bell rings again. The kid answers with an enormous bleat for such a small goat. You brush snow from its knees, scraped in the scramble on the quay. Across the slope, a herd of snowhorn goats waits on a ledge. A bell hangs from one goat's collar. Between you and the herd, a melt channel cuts through the snow.

choices.label: Look for a safe way to the herd

shelter.narration: Wind presses your wet clothes against your knees. The kid is shivering. A bank of packed snow would block the wind; a row of dark rocks would lead you nearer the bell. What do you do first?

choices.label: Make a windbreak in the snow
Use Mend to warm the kid's scraped knees

windbreak.narration: You scrape a hollow behind the bank and huddle shoulder to shoulder. The kid noses under the warmest arm. From here you can see footprints between the dark rocks, each wider than your head.

rocks.narration: The rocks give your feet something firm to find under the snow. Beside them are deep footprints. A broad wooden sledge has scraped a second track toward the bell.

mend.narration: Gentle light settles over the kid's scraped knees. It stops shaking long enough to chew the end of your sleeve. You tuck it back into your coat and find broad footprints between the rocks.

tracks.narration: A yeti herder comes around the ridge pulling an empty sledge. She stops at the sight of the kid. "There you are." Then she notices the rest of you. "There you all are. Did you come with the weather?"

choices.label: Tell her about the fold on the quay
Ask for help getting the kid home

variants.text: She looks back at your line of stones. "You marked the hollow. That will help the next person through."
She checks the kid with one broad hand. "Still warm. That long way round was well chosen."
You point out the hollow behind you. She nods. "And you found your own way out. Keep that rope."

tell_rift.narration: The yeti looks at your wet boots, then at the harbor rope. "The Exchange," she says. "That is a long way to arrive without a hat." She lays a folded blanket on the sledge. "Stand on the dark ice when I say. Walk around the white patches."

choices.label: Bring the kid to the melt channel

ask_help.narration: "First we get you warm enough to help," says the yeti. She takes a folded blanket from the sledge and wraps it around the kid and your arms together. "I keep this herd. The glacier keeps surprising me." She turns the sledge toward the melt channel.

channel.narration: Meltwater gurgles through a narrow gap. The nearest snow bridge sags when the yeti tests it. A flat stone projects farther upstream. The herder points out dark patches of ice that will hold a careful foot. The herd waits on the other side, bells clinking.

choices.label: Make a bridge with the sledge
Carry a rope across on wings
Keep everyone in step with a steady song

step.prompt: Step across the stone without slipping into the meltwater.

onSuccess.narration: You land on the far bank and pass the kid across.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips into icy water. The herder catches your wrist and lifts you onto the bank.

sledge.prompt: Hold the sledge steady while everyone crosses.

onSuccess.narration: You brace the runners against the stone. The party crawls over one at a time.

onFailure.narration: A runner slips. The herder grabs the sledge and you scramble across, soaked to the elbows.

wing_line.prompt: Wings carry the rope to the far bank. Can you guide the loose line around the sharp ice?

onSuccess.narration: You guide the line clear of sharp ice. Secured around a rock on the far bank, it steadies everyone crossing.

onFailure.narration: The line snags on sharp ice. You free it, splashing one foot into the channel.

song_step.prompt: A Songkeeper sets a steady pace. Can you lead the party along the dark patches in time with the song?

onSuccess.narration: You call the steps in time with the song. Each friend follows the herder's safe footholds.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips between two beats. The herder pulls you clear and leads the last steps herself.

dry_bank.narration: The kid sees the herd and wriggles free. A shaggy goat sniffs it from nose to tail, then nudges it firmly between her front legs. The herder checks every one of you before she smiles. "All back. Good."

wet_bank.narration: The herder wrings the edge of your sleeve out over the channel. "We will dry that indoors." The kid has already run to a shaggy goat, who sniffs it all over and refuses to let it move.

herd.narration: The herder calls the goats toward a low opening in the ice. The kid plants its feet at the entrance. From inside comes a deep note that trembles through your boots. How do you coax it in?

choices.label: Let it follow a friend's sleeve
Hum back to the low note

patient.narration: You sit in the snow beside the kid. The herd keeps walking. At last it butts your elbow, gets up, and trots after them. The herder waits for you too.

sleeve.narration: You offer a loose cuff. The kid gives it an interested nibble. The kid takes the end in its mouth and follows you through the doorway. "That coat has earned its keep," says the herder.

hum.narration: You hum the low note. The kid tilts its head. From inside the ice, another voice hums back. The kid follows the sound, and you follow the kid.

hall.narration: The doorway opens into a singing hall carved from ice. Yetis sit on benches around warm cups, holding one low note together. The herder drapes your wet things near a row of warm stones and pours tea. Damp blankets hang over a rail. "Glacier of Origins," she says. "You may stop arriving now." At the back of the hall, warm air drifts out of a glass door, and someone inside is singing scales.

choices.label: Follow the warm air to the glass door

conservatory.narration: Behind the glass door is a greenhouse, warm and damp and full of song. This school is called the Conservatory. Here students learn to be a Songkeeper, a hero who heals with songs. A yeti named Aunt Bellow conducts with a carrot. Her students sing in a row, and every plant in the room leans toward whoever is singing best. Right now the ferns lean toward a very small frogfolk at the end. Above the door hangs a song bell on a cord. A Songkeeper's songs live in that bell, and it will not ring near a thorn bracer. "Anyone who wants the bell," says Aunt Bellow, "may try it on."

variants.text: Aunt Bellow waves her carrot. "Back to the Conservatory? Good." Every plant turns, slowly, to see who has come in. The song bell waits above the door for anyone who wants to try it on.

conservatory_sing.narration: Aunt Bellow points her carrot at you. You sing. A sunflower turns its whole head to look. Then a fern. Then, very slowly, a shy little cactus. Aunt Bellow writes something on a leaf. "The cactus never turns," she whispers. "Keep singing."

listen.narration: A young yeti stops singing to turn a page in an open songbook. The note thins. Another singer joins, and it fills the hall again. The herder taps the bench beside her. "Low and steady. Try it. Nobody here learned by already knowing."

choices.label: Learn the note with the yetis
Ask what the song is for

song_answer.narration: "For listening," says the herder. She puts a hand against the wall. "A crack makes one sound. Running water makes another. The song helps us hear the difference." She hums the note once and waits for you to answer.

learn_note.narration: You find the note together. At first it shakes; then your voices settle. Across the hall, frost trembles off a sealed seam in the wall. The herder lays a palm on it, listening. "That seam was quiet yesterday."

changing.narration: "The melt is early," the herder says. "A path we used last week is water now. It led to the herd's sheltered grazing ledge. We are using stored hay while we find another way, and the pile gets smaller every day." She looks at the sealed seam. "Perhaps listening will tell us where it is safe to look." Outside, a bell rings twice. Three travelers in dark cloaks are packing their camp beside the hall.

choices.label: Help the herder dry the last blankets

variants.text: "Your windbreak is useful too," she adds. "I can tell the next travelers where to stop if the weather turns."
"And thank you for keeping everyone steady at the channel. I cannot watch every crossing now."

blankets.narration: You spread the last blanket over a rail. The herder packs a dry corner around your rope. "Bring it back if you pass this way. Bring yourselves back too." The kid bumps your knee before returning to the herd.

departure.narration: Warm and dry, you step out beside the singing hall. The kid stays with its herd. A griffin in a travel cloak is trying to fold a map while a unicorn stands on one corner. Neither has noticed that the corner is under her hoof.

variants.text: The herder lifts a hand from the newly cleared blanket rail. "Dry blankets for the next arrivals. That matters."

drift.narration: A gust wipes the footprints smooth. Ahead, a white drift fills the gap between two ridges of dark rock. The bell sounds from beyond it, but you cannot see how deep the snow is. The kid shivers against your chest. How will you get everyone through?

choices.label: Use the rope to test the drift and mark firm ground
Keep the kid tucked in and go around the rocks
Try the last place you saw the footprints

drift_probe.narration: You knot the rope around a rock and move a few steps at a time. Beneath a thin crust, the drift is hollow. You back out, find firm ground along its edge, and leave small stones marking the safe way. Beyond the ridge, the bell rings louder.

drift_detour.narration: You take turns sheltering the kid inside your coats while you follow the rocks around the drift. The walk is longer, but nobody has to test the hidden hollow. At the far ridge the kid stops shaking and pokes its nose out toward the bell.

drift_slip.narration: The crust gives under your first step. You sink to your knees, still holding the kid above the snow. Your party lays the rope across firm rock, and you pull yourself back along it. Now you can see the hollow. You skirt its edge and reach the next ridge together.

seam_response.narration: The note fades. So does the trembling under the herder's palm. A narrow line of frost has fallen to the floor beneath the sealed seam. You still remember the note. What do you try?

choices.label: Rest a hand on the ice while the others hum
Ask the herder to listen with you

seam_hum.narration: You hum. Frost ticks down the seam in time with the note. You stop; the ticking stops. When you begin again, it answers again. The ice stays shut. The herder brings her cup over and sits beside you. "Well. That was not an accident."

seam_touch.narration: You rest your hand flat on the ice. As the others hum, a faint tremble reaches your palm. It fades when they stop. You try twice more and get the same answer. The seam stays shut. "Something we can test," says the herder.

seam_listen.narration: The herder kneels beside you. You take turns humming and listening. Each time the note sounds, a low ticking answers from the seam. "We can hear that much," she says. "What lies beyond it, I do not know." The ice stays shut.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Yeti herder: Chapter-scoped female yeti herder and singer. Patient, dry humor, practical cold-weather care. Gives no complete history, prison hints, or explanation of the rifts.
npcVoices.Young yeti singer: Learns and listens; no lore lecture.
